title: Erskine Hawkins, trumpet second parts and losing his embouchure
summary: Jones says he played second trumpet parts until a prizefighter drummer, Kid Lips Hackett, led him to box, and his embouchure went.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: It came through Omaha in the thirties. Speaking about Roy Eldridge, when I saw Mr. Roy Eldridge - incidentally, he started on drums and I started on trumpet. I came out with the then Erskine Hawkins. Erskine Hawkins didn't go where I went; he went to Dozier Park.
Did you ever play with Erskine Hawkins' band?

Of course not, because when you look up and see Erskine, Erskine would be on trumpet and I would be on trumpet. Until 1930 I was playing the second part to 'Beau Koo Jack.' Of course I had to put a Coca-Cola bottle... 'Beau Koo Jack' in the key of B flat. Mr. Don Redman (HUMS) - that's on the second page and you paid 50¢ for that stack. That was a big stack. 'Beau Koo Jack' and 'Louisiana Bobo.' See I played all those things... But my embouchure went away because at the same time I had met a fellow by the name of Kid Lips Hackett and Kid Lips was a sensational drummer, but also he was a prizefighter and when the shows that he was on couldn't make their money he'd go down to the auditorium or the YMCA and get on and pick up a 20 or 25 dollars and come back to feed people, because shows would get stranded. So I was going to be a prizefighter. So there went my embouchure. But without my embouchure about losing embouchure, when I saw Mr. Louis Armstrong playing with Erskine Tate down in the theater playing his thing, I quickly gave that up!
